core_theme.question: What meaning is carried by instrumental or pseudo-semantic music, and what changes when a narrative is read in reverse?

works.display_name: Candy Dulfer & David A. Stewart - Lily Was Here

transcript_claims.film_relation_as_stated_in_transcript: Presented in the conversation as music connected to the Dutch film De Kassière / Lily Was Here.
transcript_claims.musical_structure_as_stated: A dialogue between saxophone and guitar.
emotional_reading_as_stated: guitar -> panic / pursuit / struggle / night-city tension

forward_reading_from_transcript.summary: The music was interpreted as following a difficult dramatic path of the heroine Lily and as carrying the emotional weight of loss, danger and survival.

reverse_reading.trigger: User asked: 'А если смотреть задом наперед))'
reverse_reading.summary: Reading the story backward was playfully reframed as a restorative narrative: problems with the law unwind, injuries disappear, the lost beloved returns, and tension transforms into movement toward safety and calm.

transcript_claims.language_description_as_stated: pseudo-Latin / invented language used primarily as a musical-sonic layer rather than a literal text carrier

clip_plot_as_stated.historical_inspiration_claimed_in_transc: Cathar-related inspiration was attributed to the project creator in the conversation

events: the manuscript survives attempted destruction and reaches later times
continuity / transmission through the ages is emphasized
a woman holding a newborn child appears as a symbol of rebirth / a new cycle
characters and/or choral figures are described as dissolving into light
clip_ending_as_described_in_transcript.interpretive_summary: The ending was presented as preservation of knowledge across destruction, followed by renewal and continuity.

semantic_synthesis.forward_lane: Music can carry an emotional or narrative map even when literal verbal semantics are absent or intentionally blurred.
semantic_synthesis.reverse_lane: Reversing event order can transform a tragedy-shaped sequence into a restoration-shaped sequence without changing the underlying events themselves.
